guardian.title: Uganda to withdraw from Invictus Games ‘out of respect for King Charles’, says military chief
guardian.description:
Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba announces decision to pull out in post on X, citing tensions over ‘Harry-Meghan nonsense’

Uganda is withdrawing from the Duke of Sussex’s Invictus Games, the country’s military chief has said, out of respect for King Charles amid division over the “Harry-Meghan nonsense”.

Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, son of the Ugandan president, made the surprise announcement in a post on X on Wednesday.

guardian.description:
Key regions of the brain linked to movement, learning and emotions were affected and may lead to cognitive problems

Babies born to mothers with anaemia have smaller brains, particularly in key regions linked to movement, learning and the regulation of emotion, according to a study.

Researchers said the differences, first detected at the age of one, could lead to cognitive problems when children started school.

guardian.description:
Sarah Khalifa, 39, charged with forming organised criminal gang to manufacture and traffic drugs

An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drug case, official media reported on Saturday.

The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.

The family of a British father who was found dead in the Caribbean in January is urging authorities in Grenada to work with UK police to uncover the truth about his death.

Andrew Frederick’s body was found in the property he was staying at in Grenada on 4 January. An autopsy, performed in the same week by a privately hired pathologist, concluded that the 47-year-old’s death was a homicide.

rfi.title: Mao still revered in China as criticism remains risky 50 years on
rfi.description: Fifty years after Mao Zedong's death, his image and ideas remain deeply embedded in China, where his portrait still dominates Tiananmen Square in the heart of Beijing and Communist Party rhetoric continues to draw on his thinking. For older Chinese people, revolutionary songs keep memories of his era alive, while younger generations see him as a more distant historical figure. Openly criticising his legacy, however, remains difficult.

lemonde.description: A l’approche de l’élection de 2027, un ouvrage écrit par un collectif de chercheurs et de journalistes dresse une radiographie singulière de la société française en mesurant différents phénomènes. Plutôt que de raconter une France fracturée, les auteurs dépeignent d’abord un pays riche en contradictions.

france24fr.title: B. Netanyahu : une résilience sans faille ?
france24fr.description: En Israël, à 7 semaines des élections législatives, une publication de Haaretz relance la polémique autour de B. Netanyahu. S’appuyant sur un livre à paraître, le quotidien affirme que le Premier ministre aurait été informé par les Émirats arabes unis, dix jours avant le 7 octobre, d’une opération majeure du Hamas. Le cabinet du Premier ministre dénonce des accusations "totalement mensongères". L’opposition réclame des explications alors que la campagne électorale s’intensifie.

france24fr.title: Législatives en Israël : "Le 7-Octobre s’impose comme la ligne de partage de la campagne"
france24fr.description: À l’approche des élections législatives d’octobre, le traumatisme du massacre du 7-Octobre se retrouve au centre de la campagne, ravivant la question des responsabilités de Benjamin Netanyahu et les appels de l’opposition à une commission d’enquête d’État. Les révélations sur les alertes qui auraient précédé l’attaque, comme les accusations de "complot" venues du camp du Premier ministre, peuvent-elles fragiliser son emprise sur une partie de son électorat ?

france24fr.title: Cameroun : Maurice Kamto démissionne de la présidence de son parti
france24fr.description: 🇨🇲 Au Cameroun, Maurice Kamto quitte la présidence de son parti, le MRC. L’opposant a annoncé sa démission mardi, sur fond de fronde interne. Un départ simultané à celui de son son premier vice-président Mamadu Mota, qui fragilise encore le parti à l’approche des échéances électorales de 2027.

france24fr.title: Ballon d'Or 2026 : qui soulèvera le trophée ?
france24fr.description: La course au Ballon d’Or est lancée !⚽️ Messi, Mbappé, Yamal, Haaland, Kane, Dembélé, Vinícius Jr… Les plus grandes stars du football sont en course pour décrocher le prestigieux trophée. Découvrez les joueurs nommés en mettant en pause l'écran et dites-nous en commentaire qui mérite de soulever le trophée cette année !

france24fr.title: Élections en Russie : les 1 001 tours de passe-passe pour éliminer les candidats encombrants
france24fr.description: Le pouvoir russe multiplie les motifs fallacieux pour disqualifier des candidats qui avaient pourtant obtenu le feu vert pour participer aux élections législatives organisées du 18 au 20 septembre. La guerre en Ukraine rend les autorités toujours plus frileuses quant à celles et ceux qui peuvent se présenter.

france24fr.title: Ballon d'Or 2026 : qui succédera à Ousmane Dembélé ?
france24fr.description: La liste des nommés a été dévoilée. Kylian Mbappé, Lionel Messi ou encore Ousmane Dembélé figurent parmi les 30 joueurs sélectionnés pour le Ballon d'or 2026 qui sera attribué le 26 octobre. Et vous, qui voyez-vous soulever le trophée ?

france24fr.title: La France se prépare à la première visite d'un pape depuis 18 ans
france24fr.description: Un engouement populaire prend place autour de la visite du pape en France, prévue du 25 au 28 septembre prochain. Plus d'un million de personnes sont attendues pour les quatre grands rendez-vous de Léon XIV. La conférence des évêques de France table sur 27 millions d'euros de dépense et lance un appel aux dons.

france24fr.title: Rwanda : une femme arrêtée pour une robe jugée "trop courte"
france24fr.description: La vidéo de l'arrestation d'une jeune femme, pour sa tenue jugée "indécente" par des autorités rwandaises, a été republiée un nombre incalculable de fois sur les réseaux sociaux. La police a finalement présenté ses excuses, affirmant que les agents concernés avaient été arrêtés et que la jeune femme avait été libérée.

france24fr.title: Plastique: le gouvernement français recule sur la consigne des bouteilles
france24fr.description: Le gouvernement français renonce à imposer la consigne obligatoire pour les bouteilles en plastique. Les collectivités territoriales y étaient opposées. Elles n'auraient plus pu revendre ces bouteilles à des centres de recyclage et ainsi financer la collecte des déchets. La France doit toujours trouver un moyen d'augmenter son taux de recyclage. Tant qu'elle n'y parvient pas, elle doit s'acquitter d'une amende de 1,5 milliard d'euros par an auprès de l'Union Européenne.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : l'information en péril ?
france24fr.description: Condamné à 1 an de prison, le journaliste Haythem El Mekki est en exil en France. Selon lui, le pouvoir ne veut "qu'aucune voix critique ou dissidente ne reste en liberté". Il témoigne en plateau sur France 24.

france24fr.title: Le RN exclut un policier membre de son service d’ordre après des propos racistes et complotistes
france24fr.description: Après la diffusion d'une vidéo dans laquelle un policier municipal de Carcassonne tient des propos racistes, misogynes et complotistes, le Rassemblement national a annoncé mercredi l'exclusion immédiate de l'agent qui était encarté dans le parti d'extrême droite.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : Dette, FMI et vie chère, le Premier ministre décline ses priorités à l'Assemblée
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Au Sénégal, le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô a défendu ce mardi sa politique et l’accord avec le FMI devant l’Assemblée nationale. Sans évoquer de motion de défiance, le président de l'Assemblée nationale, Ousmane Sonko annonce un contrôle parlementaire des accords.

france24fr.title: France : le prix du carburant au plus haut depuis le début de la guerre au Moyen-Orient
france24fr.description: Une nouvelle réunion s'est tenue ce matin au ministère de l'économie face à l'urgence, car l'essence n'a jamais été aussi chère. Pour beaucoup de français, la situation est devenue intenable. Le gouvernement maintient sa position et reste "défavorable" à des mesures d'aide "plus générales".

france24fr.title: Colonisation en Cisjordanie : Israël annonce 1 000 nouvelles habitations
france24fr.description: La justice israélienne a rejeté, mardi 8 septembre, un recours visant à stopper l'avancement du vaste projet E1, qui prévoit d'étendre la colonisation en Cisjordanie. La proposition est vivement critiquée par plusieurs ONG et pays occidentaux. Des explications de Jean-Paul Chagnollaud, professeur émérite et président d’honneur de l’Institut de recherche et études Méditerranée Moyen-Orient.

france24fr.title: "Je ne me sens plus en sécurité" : au Kenya, l'inquiétude des commerçants burundais
france24fr.description: Depuis les déclarations du président kényan William Ruto, lundi, stigmatisant les travailleurs étrangers, les Burundais manifestent leur colère. Ils sont 16 000 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile burundais à vivre au Kenya, et beaucoup survivent grâce à des emplois dans le secteur informel. La très grande majorité d'entre eux cherche désormais à quitter le territoire.

france24fr.title: Camille Cottin et sa bande de retour dans "Dix pour cent, le film"
france24fr.description: Au programme de ce numéro 100 % cinéma de "À l'Affiche !" : "Dix pour cent, le film" d'Émilie Noblet. Six ans après la sortie de la quatrième saison de "Dix pour cent", les agents et leurs talents reviennent pour un film disponible sur Netflix. Camille Cottin, Laure Calamy, Grégory Montel, Nicolas Maury...toute la bande est là avec en "guest-stars" : George Clooney, Eva Longoria, Vincent Macaigne et Laetitia Casta.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : manifestations pour la libération du journaliste Mohamed Yousfi
france24fr.description: 🇹🇳 En Tunisie, les journalistes se mobilisent après l’arrestation de leur confrère Mohamed Yousfi. Interpellé vendredi avant une émission sur la crise de l’eau, il est soupçonné de blanchiment d’argent. Un mandat de dépôt a été émis contre lui mardi.

france24fr.title: Sanctions contre Israël : 12 personnalités britanniques interdites d'entrée sur le territoire
france24fr.description: Le Royaume-Uni, la France, le Canada et huit autres pays ont annoncé, mardi 8 septembre, qu'ils allaient sanctionner le commerce avec les colonies israéliennes en Cisjordanie, durcissant le ton face à Israël. L'État hébreu a riposté en annonçant la fermeture du consulat britannique à Jérusalem. Depuis, douze représentants britanniques ont l'interdiction d'entrer en Israël. Décryptage avec Anne Corpet, chroniqueuse internationale France 24.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Tanker mit irakischem Öl gerät ins Kreuzfeuer

nzz.description: Die Adus-Klinik in Dielsdorf schien Anfang 2022 dem Untergang geweiht. Jetzt bekommt sie ihren Leistungsauftrag vom Kanton zurück.

spiegel.description: Ein Bericht bringt Benjamin Netanyahu vor der Wahl in Israel in Bedrängnis. Die Emirate sollen den Premier vor einem Angriff der Hamas gewarnt haben. Für die Opposition sind die Recherchen ein Geschenk.

spiegel.description: Porsche hat seine Anteile an der Luxusmarke Bugatti sowie am E-Auto-Hersteller Rimac verkauft. Das erlöste Geld braucht das angeschlagene Unternehmen unter anderem für Pensionsverpflichtungen.

spiegel.description: Wenn Sachsen-Anhalt seit der Wahl blau ist, dann ist die Gemeinde Schnaudertal dunkelblau. Hier, tief im Süden des Landes, haben teilweise 75 Prozent für die AfD gestimmt. Warum?

spiegel.description: Als »Checker Tobi« erklärt Tobias Krell Kindern die Welt. Was sagt der Ersatzlehrer der Nation zur Bildungsmisere?

spiegel.description: Nach dem verheerenden Flugzeugunglück von Miami offenbart die Auswertung des Flugschreibers eine Reihe ungewöhnlicher Ereignisse bei der Landung. Der Luftsicherheitsexperte Thomas Friesacher vermutet eine »Verkettung von Pilotenfehlern«.

spiegel.description: Von »positives Gefühl« bis »Zäsur«: Bundestagsabgeordnete reagieren sehr unterschiedlich auf das AfD-Ergebnis in Sachsen-Anhalt.

spiegel.description: Die Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt gegen Steffen Krach, der für die SPD für das Amt des Regierenden Bürgermeisters in Berlin kandidiert. Es geht um den Verdacht der Bestechlichkeit. Nun hat Krach sich erstmals geäußert.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Mutter berichtet vom Tod ihres Sohnes durch russischen Angriff
spiegel.description: Am 20. August trafen russische Raketen und Drohnen Kyjiw. Mindestens 17 Menschen kamen ums Leben, darunter der 29-jährige Yevhenii Ionov. Seine Mutter hatte bis zuletzt auf seine Rettung gehofft.

spiegel.title: Norwegen: Beisetzung von König Harald V. in Oslo
spiegel.description: Er war Europas ältester amtierender Monarch und galt den Norwegern als »Großvater der Nation«. Jetzt wurde König Harald V. von Norwegen in Oslo beigesetzt. Die Trauerfeier in Bildern.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Generaldebatte im Bundestag, Zollstreit USA gegen Kanada, Benjamin Netanyahu gegen »Haaretz«
spiegel.description: Die Generaldebatte im Bundestag gerät zur Abrechnung zwischen Regierung und Opposition. Kanada lächelt Wüterich Trump beiseite, und Netanyahu will »Haaretz« wegen einer belastenden Recherche verklagen. Das ist die Lage am Mittwochabend.

spiegel.title: Weltraumgipfel in Paris: Warum dem Westen Trägerraketen fehlen
spiegel.description: Deutschland will im Weltall aufrüsten, doch die globale Raumfahrt steuert auf eine massive Krise zu. Elon Musk will die wichtigste Rakete für den Satellitentransport ausmustern – und echte Alternativen fehlen.

spiegel.description: Der Schock am Wahlabend, die ratlose Politikerrunde, der Reflex, sich noch einmal zu erklären – was nach dem AfD-Erfolg passierte, kennt man in Österreich schon lange. Die Ratlosigkeit danach ist das eigentliche Problem.

phys-org.title: You can't shield kids from scary news—here's what 'Sesame Street' and other children's shows did after 9/11
phys-org.description: On back-to-school night in 2005, I eagerly entered my youngest child's first-grade classroom. The walls were festooned with brightly colored responses to the prompt: "Draw something you remember."

phys-org.title: AI reveals new class of cellular 'off switch' linked to cancer pathways
phys-org.description: Cornell researchers have used artificial intelligence to uncover a previously unknown way cells control how proteins move inside them, a process essential for growth, communication and movement that is often disrupted in cancer.

phys-org.title: Body-related TikTok content linked to self-objectification and mood
phys-org.description: Viewing "thinspiration" content on TikTok increases self-objectification and worsens mood, while viewing body-positive content also increases self-objectification but is linked to a more positive mood, according to a new study published in PLOS One by Samantha Jones of Western University, Canada, and colleagues.

phys-org.title: 'Here, There and Everywhere': The Beatles have permeated research papers across academic disciplines
phys-org.description: More than 3,000 scientific article titles across disciplines have made use of Beatles song titles and lyrics, according to a study published in PLOS One by Gabriel Budel of Delft University of Technology in the Netherlands and colleagues. This analysis is an unprecedentedly large-scale, cross-disciplinary account of how the Beatles have left their mark on scientific writing.

phys-org.title: Fossils from embryo to adult suggest how an enigmatic, bird-like troodontid dinosaur grew
phys-org.description: Analysis of fossilized remains from dinosaurs known as troodontids reveals how one species' hip and leg bones may have developed over its lifespan, from embryo to adult—with potential implications for resolving longstanding taxonomic challenges. David Varricchio of Montana State University, U.S., and Heath Caldwell of North Carolina State University, U.S., present their findings in the journal PLOS One on Sept. 9, 2026.

phys-org.title: Asian elephants can resist impulsive behavior, researchers find
phys-org.description: Researchers at the CUNY Graduate Center and Hunter College have found that Asian elephants can suppress impulsive behaviors and adjust their actions when circumstances change—a cognitive ability that may help explain the animals' sophisticated problem-solving skills and social behavior.

phys-org.title: JWST discovers that Chariklo's invisible rings are changing
phys-org.description: Until just over a decade ago, ring systems were thought to be exclusive to the giant planets of the solar system, such as Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. However, in 2013, a small body barely 250 kilometers (155 miles) in diameter, located at nearly 17 times the Earth–sun distance, joined this small group. The object is Chariklo, a small body orbiting between Saturn and Uranus, around which astronomers discovered two dense rings.

phys-org.title: Ice Age origins of one of humanity's oldest drug habits discovered
phys-org.description: A team of Griffith University archaeologists has uncovered evidence that humans were using mind-altering substances much earlier than previously supposed.

phys-org.title: Decades-old DNA mystery solved after strands are captured zipping together for the first time
phys-org.description: Researchers have captured the moment two DNA molecules zip together, overcoming their identical negative charges to pair up and revealing a mechanism that has puzzled scientists for more than 20 years. Using high-powered atomic force microscopy, scientists at the University of Sheffield and the University of York directly imaged two DNA double helices locking together, marking the first time this fundamental biological process has been visualized.

phys-org.title: Liquid gold: Could we turn our urine into fertilizer?
phys-org.description: For thousands of years, human urine has had real value. After our bodies absorb nutrients from our food, they excrete the rest—mainly via urine. An adult produces about 500 liters (132 gallons) a year. This liquid gold is very rich in nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, three nutrients vital for plant growth.

phys-org.title: Survey shows public confidence in Fauci declines since spring but still exceeds RFK Jr.
phys-org.description: Americans' confidence in Dr. Anthony Fauci as a source of trustworthy public health information declined over the four months from April to August 2026 in a survey conducted after he appeared before the U.S. Senate Homeland Security Committee but declined to answer its questions, invoking his Fifth Amendment protection against self-incrimination.

phys-org.title: The Anthropocene was rejected as a geological epoch—but the idea is still changing how we see the world
phys-org.description: The Anthropocene became part of the zeitgeist after Nobel laureate Paul Crutzen launched the idea in 2000. This is the notion that a crescendo of human impacts has recently propelled Earth out of the relatively stable climatic conditions of the Holocene epoch, during which human civilization developed and flourished, to produce a new kind of planet.

phys-org.title: The surprising place where giant dinosaurs incubated their eggs
phys-org.description: Finding a fossilized dinosaur egg is exceptionally rare, but finding a stash of more than 250 shell fragments in the chilly southern reaches of the planet is even more surprising. The discoveries come from southernmost Patagonia in Argentina, where giant, long-necked titanosaurs roamed toward the end of the dinosaur era. Previous egg discoveries suggested that these massive beasts usually nested much farther north.

phys-org.title: Canada's last epishelf lake is gone for good, study confirms
phys-org.description: Canada's last epishelf lake drained into the Arctic Ocean following the 2020 breakup of the Milne Ice Shelf and will not recover, a new study confirms.

phys-org.title: When benefit corporations get certified, is it 'greenwashing' in stereo?
phys-org.description: The term "benefit corporation" is becoming increasingly familiar as a label for companies with a hybrid commitment to the social good and profit-making. Interestingly, the term itself has taken on a hybrid meaning.

phys-org.title: Restoring Australia's she-oaks means listening to Indigenous knowledges
phys-org.description: In Australia, many Indigenous communities have connections and stories linked to the she-oak.

phys-org.title: Tiny 2D cracks creep through materials before triggering sudden fracture, experiments reveal
phys-org.description: We have all seen something suddenly break: a phone screen cracks, a plastic object snaps or a piece of glass shatters. To our eyes, the failure seems to happen all at once. But what if the most important part of the break happens long before the final snap?

phys-org.title: The 'costly son' hypothesis: Why bigger sons may make births riskier across species
phys-org.description: A new comparative review, published in The Anatomical Record, examines factors that may lead to birth complications among humans and other mammals. The study suggests that fetal sex may play an important role in risky births in humans and several other species.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

proj-syn.title: How 9/11 Fractured the Global Order
proj-syn.description: The terrorist attack on the United States 25 years ago remains among the most consequential events of this century. By fundamentally altering the trajectories of the United States and Russia, as well as that of a rising China, al-Qaeda’s attack set in motion developments that would produce the geopolitical tumult we live in today.

proj-syn.title: China’s Permanent Manufacturing Revolution
proj-syn.description: In developed economies, manufacturing employment will decline, regardless of industrial strategies pursued. China's competitiveness means that any expectation that manufacturing will absorb more than a trivial fraction of the large increases in the working-age population still occurring in India or Africa is a delusion.

proj-syn.title: Europe Needs Dual-Use Defense Spending
proj-syn.description: Some EU countries, such as Poland, are using their expanded defense budgets to buy more foreign hardware. A better approach would be to foster a thriving innovation ecosystem which ensures that the technologies, institutions, and people that underpin a strong military benefit the civilian economy as well.

proj-syn.title: The World 9/11 Didn’t Make
proj-syn.description: Looking back at the past quarter-century, it becomes apparent that the 9/11 terrorist attack against the United States was not a transformative event. Far more important developments have intervened, not least America’s rejection of the postwar order that it had a large hand in building.

proj-syn.title: The BRICS at 20
proj-syn.description: If the promise of the BRICS was to establish a monetary union, a single market, or a tightly integrated political alliance, it has not been fulfilled. But if it was to build a platform for emerging economies to cooperate while advancing their own strategic autonomy, the BRICS has exceeded expectations.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Security Depends on a Clear Electrification Target
proj-syn.description: The politics around electrification are beginning to shift in Europe as more people recognize its importance for economic competitiveness and industrial resilience. European Union policymakers should seize this momentum to embed a binding target of at least 50% electrification by 2040 in the bloc’s energy security framework.

proj-syn.title: The AI Race Could Sink US-China Détente
proj-syn.description: The competition between the United States and China to develop AI and deploy it globally poses the biggest threat to the two countries’ currently constructive relations. Without an ongoing AI dialogue to avoid escalation, a return to the zero-sum conflict that rattled both sides last year cannot be ruled out.

proj-syn.title: Are China’s Rare Earths Really a Potent Weapon?
proj-syn.description: The available evidence indicates that Chinese rare-earth export restrictions would cost the West far less than often feared, though this cost is impossible to estimate precisely in advance. This is forcing prudence on both sides, to the disappointment of geopolitical hawks and the benefit of the global economy.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Shock in East Asia
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump has alarmed his East Asian allies by canceling two joint military exercises with South Korea, a move that seems motivated less by whim than by a fondness for tyrants. The question now is whether South Korea and Japan will set aside historical resentments for the sake of mutual interests.

proj-syn.title: Building a Resilient Nepal
proj-syn.description: After Japan’s 2011 Fukushima nuclear disaster, the Japanese government changed the building codes for schools and housing and rethought the placement of critical infrastructure. Nepal (and other vulnerable countries) must pursue a similar approach.

proj-syn.title: Unpaid Work in the AI Age
proj-syn.description: Unpaid work, such as dealing with government bureaucracy and private-sector administration, consumes a huge amount of people's free time. While AI tools have the potential to change this, with important implications for the economy, predictions about AI’s impact tend to focus exclusively on paid work.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Wellness Industry Is Hijacking Women’s Health
proj-syn.description: Menopause and perimenopause, long under-researched and dismissed, have become a growth industry for online advertisers and wellness companies. Mining intimate data, this lucrative digital ecosystem exploits medical uncertainty to sell women hormones and supplements they don't need, or that can even harm them.

proj-syn.title: Who Controls the Data Controls the Future
proj-syn.description: While AI is becoming increasingly central to finance, defense, health care, and public administration, it depends on resources most governments do not control: the data used to train it and the compute that processes it. Unless this changes, countries will remain subject to decisions made in boardrooms they cannot influence.

proj-syn.title: Will Europe Be as Unprepared as Ukraine Was?
proj-syn.description: With Russia ramping up its hybrid war, Europe must choose. It can invest in its own defense, accept the trade-offs involved, and build credible deterrence, or it can continue to underspend, hope that diplomacy will suffice, assume that US protection will always be available, and tell itself that the war in Ukraine is a local affair.

proj-syn.title: The Case for a Cashflow Tax
proj-syn.description: In the context of the US economy, a cashflow tax would offer far-reaching benefits in promoting economic growth, taxing rents, and raising incremental revenue efficiently. Moreover, well-known concerns about complexity and fairness are easily addressed.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh’s Best Move Is to Do Nothing
proj-syn.description: Beholden to mainstream economic ideas, the new US Federal Reserve chair has committed himself, and his reputation, to a goal he cannot achieve. Reining in inflation requires not interest-rate adjustments but much larger strategic shifts that are not within the Fed’s power to influence.

proj-syn.title: How Developing Countries Can Do More With Less
proj-syn.description: Evaluation frameworks for development projects have long been influenced by donor priorities. But foreign-aid cuts have created an opportunity for African countries to implement equitable evaluation practices, both to channel limited resources more effectively and to shape the future of global development governance.

proj-syn.title: America’s Naval Disaster
proj-syn.description: Plagued by exorbitant costs and chronic delays, American shipbuilders cannot produce enough vessels to keep pace with China. US President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the industry does little to address its underlying problems and threatens to squander hundreds of billions of dollars.
